Proposition
[Iterated Leibniz Rule Along One Axis]

↗ def:partial-derivative

\group Multiindex Calculus

For smooth $u,v : \R ^n \to \R $, an axis $i$, and $m\in \N $, \[ \partial _{x_i}^m(uv)=\sum _{j=0}^m\binom {m}{j} (\partial _{x_i}^j u)(\partial _{x_i}^{m-j}v). \]
Proof

\sketch Restrict to the line $\gamma (t)=x+te_i$. The chain rule identifies the $k$th derivatives of the restrictions of $u$, $v$, and $uv$ with the $k$th $x_i$-derivatives. Applying the one-variable Leibniz rule at $t=0$ gives the formula at $x$.

□
